ios.desc:
That "fast" charging cable might just be standard speed. Your expensive external SSD might be throttled by a bad cable. USB Connection Information helps you verify the real performance of your devices USB and lightning connections.

STOP GUESSING. START KNOWING.

Verify the actual transfer speeds of your connected external drives and estimate the real wattage reaching your battery. Perfect for anyone who's ever wondered "is this cable actually fast?" or "is this charger working properly?"

CORE FEATURES
- Data Speed Testing: Measure actual read and write speeds of external USB and Lightning drives to ensure your storage isn't bottlenecked.
- Charging Speed & Voltage Fingerprinting: Calculate the actual wattage reaching your battery and use unique charging fingerprinting to estimate the specific USB-PD voltage rail (e.g., 5V, 9V, 15V) powering your device.
- Charging Curve Logging: Chart your entire charging session to see how power delivery changes as the battery fills.
- Device Capability Identification: See the exact maximum data speeds and charging wattage your specific iPhone or iPad model supports.
- Detailed Drive Info: View connected volume names, file system formats, and total/available capacities.
- Test History: Save and review past test results to compare different drives, cables, and chargers.

BUILT FOR YOUR WORKFLOW
- Simple, one-tap testing for both data speeds and charging rates.
- Intelligent warnings to prevent testing internal storage by mistake or causing excessive drive wear.
- Clear visualizations for your connection speed (e.g. USB 2.0 vs USB 3.0).


EFFICIENT & PRIVATE 
Native SwiftUI app with minimal resource usage. Your data never leaves your device: no tracking, no telemetry, and no cloud sync.

TECHNICAL NOTE 
Due to iOS system limitations, charging wattage is estimated by measuring battery percentage changes over time. This represents the actual power reaching the battery rather than the total charger output. For the most accurate results, run charging tests when your battery is between 20% and 50% and screen brightness is low.

quotes.text:
Like many of you, I've collected a drawer full of USB-C cables over the years. And like many of you, I've experienced the frustration of plugging in a "fast" external SSD, only to see abysmal transfer speeds. Recently, I got a new SSD, excited to finally get some quick backups going. Plugged it in, started copying, and watched the progress show hours for a few GB. My immediate thought: DOA drive, or worse, I was scammed.

After some head scratching and cable swapping, I discovered the culprit: a USB-C cable that was only negotiating USB 2.0 speeds. It looked identical to my other cables, but its internal wiring was effectively throttling my transfer rates. It's a common problem, made worse by the visually similar USB-C cables despite their vast range of capabilities.

I knew macOS's System Information panel could show me the current USB connection speed, but digging through that every time I connected a new device or swapped a cable was just too much friction for my workflow. I figured there had to be a better way.

So, I decided to build it. I've developed several Mac apps in Swift before, but this was my first dive into menu bar applications and background processes. It was a fun challenge to integrate with the system in a lightweight, background application format.

The result is USB Connection Information. It's a small menu bar app that displays the active USB connection speed for your devices at a glance. It shows speed, USB version, wattage, device manufacturer, and …
